label: Mohenjo-daro's drains
detail: Mohenjo-daro in the Indus Valley flourishes from about 2500 BC with grid streets and covered brick street drains.

label: Aqua Appia
detail: Rome's first aqueduct is commissioned by the censor Appius Claudius Caecus.

label: Great Fire of London
detail: The fire starts in a Pudding Lane bakery and destroys 13,200 houses and 87 parish churches.

label: Rebuilding of London Act
detail: The act favors brick and stone, regulates street widths and bans overhanging upper floors. (Named the 1666 Act; royal assent came in February 1667.)

label: Gas lamps on Pall Mall
detail: Frederick Winsor lights London's Pall Mall with gas, using old musket barrels as pipes.

label: Gas lights Pall Mall
detail: Frederick Albert Winsor gives the first public demonstration of gas street lighting on Pall Mall, London, using old musket barrels as pipes.

label: First gas company chartered
detail: London's Gas Light and Coke Company, the world's first gas company, receives a royal charter.

label: 20,000 pigs eat New York's garbage
detail: About 20,000 pigs roam New York's streets, roughly one per five residents, eating organic waste.

label: Boston Gas Light Company chartered
detail: Boston charters its first gas company.

label: Boston's first gas street lamp
detail: Boston lights its first public gas street lamp in Dock Square, near Faneuil Hall.

label: Croton Aqueduct opens
detail: New York's gravity-fed Croton Aqueduct begins service; its reservoirs about 60 feet above the city push water to roughly the sixth story.

label: New York removes its street pigs
detail: After a cholera epidemic, the city finally corrals the pigs, 5,000 to 6,000 by June 1849.

label: Boston fire alarm telegraph
detail: Boston opens the first municipal electric fire alarm telegraph, with 40 street boxes.

label: Broad Street cholera outbreak
detail: A Soho outbreak kills about 500 people in 10 days; John Snow traces it to a single water pump.

label: Back Bay filling begins
detail: Boston begins filling the polluted Back Bay with gravel brought by rail from Needham.

label: The Great Stink
detail: A foul summer on the Thames leads to Joseph Bazalgette's intercepting sewers.

label: Bazalgette's sewers begin
detail: London starts building Joseph Bazalgette's intercepting sewers, completed in 1875, a combined system that overflows to the Thames.

label: London's first underground railway
detail: The Metropolitan Railway opens between Paddington and Farringdon. (date disputed: January 9 or 10)

label: First traffic signal, London
detail: A gas-lit semaphore signal by John Peake Knight goes up outside the Houses of Parliament; it explodes in 1869. (date disputed: 9 or 10 December)

label: Great Boston Fire
detail: The fire burns about 65 acres and 776 buildings downtown, helped by weak water pressure and locked alarm boxes.

label: Gamewell factory in Newton Highlands
detail: Gamewell and Kennard open a fire alarm factory, turning Boston's invention into a national industry.

label: Electric arc lights in Paris
detail: Paris installs electric street lights on the avenue de l'Opera.

label: Cleveland's arc lights
detail: Cleveland demonstrates 12 arc lights around Public Square.

label: New York district steam begins
detail: The New York Steam Company begins service in Manhattan; it merges into Con Edison in 1954.

label: Pearl Street Station
detail: Edison's central station begins supplying lower Manhattan with direct current.

label: Gamewell in 250 cities
detail: Gamewell fire alarm systems run in more than 250 US and Canadian cities.

label: Richmond electric streetcars
detail: Frank Sprague's Richmond system becomes the model for electric street railways, including Boston's.

label: First rooftop tank firm
detail: Isseks Brothers is founded, the first company formed specifically to build New York's rooftop water tanks.

label: Waring takes over NYC street cleaning
detail: Sanitary engineer George E. Waring Jr. arrives; his first step is a law requiring horses and carts to be stabled overnight.

label: First US subway
detail: Boston's Tremont Street Subway opens from Park Street to Boylston; more than 100,000 ride on day one.

label: First US subway opens in Boston
detail: The Tremont Street Subway opens at Boylston and Park Street; more than 100,000 people ride on day one.

label: Waring dies
detail: Waring dies of yellow fever contracted while studying sanitation in Cuba.

label: Electric signal tested in Cleveland
detail: A red and green electric signal is tested at Euclid Avenue and East 105th Street, switched by hand from a booth.

label: First interconnected signals
detail: Salt Lake City links six intersections to one manual switch.

label: Three-color signal in Detroit
detail: William Potts' three-color, four-direction signal is installed at Woodward Avenue and Fort Street.

label: Garrett Morgan's signal patent
detail: Morgan receives US Patent 1,475,024 for a hand-cranked three-position signal with an all-stop position; it was not the first traffic light.

label: Britain's first permanent automatic signals
detail: Automatic signals are installed permanently at Park Row and Bond Street in Leeds.

label: NYC incinerators peak
detail: New York runs 21 municipal incinerators; only ten remain by 1946.

label: 999 launches in London
detail: The world's first emergency telephone number, prompted by a fatal 1935 Marylebone fire.

label: Quabbin towns dissolved
detail: Dana, Enfield, Greenwich and Prescott, Massachusetts, are disincorporated at midnight to make way for the Quabbin Reservoir; about 2,500 people are displaced.

label: Quabbin Reservoir full
detail: The reservoir that drowned four Massachusetts towns is declared full; it supplies 46 metro Boston communities.

label: Fresh Kills opens
detail: The first garbage scow arrives at Fresh Kills on Staten Island, a landfill meant to be temporary.

label: GM and partners convicted
detail: A federal jury convicts GM, Firestone, Standard Oil of California, Phillips and Mack of conspiring to monopolize bus sales to National City Lines companies, and acquits them on transit ownership.

label: One computer, 120 signals
detail: Denver uses a single computer to control 120 traffic lights.

label: Federal-Aid Highway Act
detail: The US authorizes over 41,000 miles of interstates with 90% federal funding.

label: Congress orders bridge inspection standards
detail: The Federal-Aid Highway Act directs the creation of national bridge inspection standards.

label: First 911 call
detail: Rankin Fite calls Tom Bevill in Haleyville, Alabama, on the Alabama Telephone Company network.

label: First NBIS published
detail: The first National Bridge Inspection Standards create the first nationally coordinated US bridge inspection program.

label: Clean Water Act
detail: Congress passes amendments requiring permits for pipe discharges and funding sewage plants, over President Nixon's veto.

label: Roosevelt Island trash tubes open
detail: An Envac pneumatic system begins moving trash at 60 to 70 mph through 20-inch tubes.

label: SCATS developed in Sydney
detail: The New South Wales Department of Main Roads develops SCATS, one of the first commercially available adaptive signal systems.

label: Right turn on red goes national
detail: The Energy Policy and Conservation Act ties federal energy aid to states allowing right turn on red.

label: BWSC created
detail: The Massachusetts legislature creates the Boston Water and Sewer Commission, a body separate from the city that sets its own rates.

label: SCOOT developed in the UK
detail: The Transport Research Laboratory develops SCOOT adaptive control for the Department of Transport.

label: Proposition 2½ approved
detail: Massachusetts voters cap property tax levy growth at 2.5% a year plus new construction; the law took effect in FY1982.

label: Quincy sues over Boston Harbor
detail: The city of Quincy sues over harbor pollution, followed by the Conservation Law Foundation and the US government.

label: MWRA created
detail: The Massachusetts Water Resources Authority splits off from the Metropolitan District Commission to run wholesale water and sewage treatment.

label: MWRA takes over
detail: The new Massachusetts Water Resources Authority takes over Greater Boston's water and sewer systems.

label: Boston Harbor court schedule
detail: Federal Judge A. David Mazzone sets a 13-year construction schedule for cleaning up Boston Harbor.

label: Deer Island schedule ordered
detail: Federal Judge A. David Mazzone orders a 13-year schedule to build the Deer Island treatment plant.

label: "Harbor of shame"
detail: George H.W. Bush tours Boston Harbor and calls it a "harbor of shame" in the presidential race against Michael Dukakis.

label: Sludge dumping ends
detail: Sludge discharges to Boston Harbor end; sludge goes to a Fore River plant to become fertilizer pellets.

label: EU adopts 112
detail: Council Decision 91/396/EEC makes 112 the single European emergency number alongside national numbers.

label: NEMA TS 2 standard
detail: The TS 2 controller standard adds a serial data link and defines coordination and preemption.

label: South Korea adopts designated bags
detail: South Korea introduces designated garbage bags; food waste recycling is 2% that year.

label: Baltimore launches 311
detail: The first 311 line opens to divert police non-emergency calls.

label: Ampelmännchen saved
detail: A citizen campaign wins the right to keep East Berlin's walking-man signal, which becomes a registered trademark.

label: FCC reserves 311
detail: FCC 97-51 assigns 311 nationwide for non-emergency government services, and 711 for relay services.

label: First ASCE Report Card
detail: The American Society of Civil Engineers begins grading US infrastructure.

label: Transport for London created
detail: TfL is created under the Greater London Authority Act 1999, with a board appointed and chaired by the Mayor of London.

label: Deer Island outfall finished
detail: The MWRA completes a deep-water sewage outfall as part of the Boston Harbor cleanup.

label: Deer Island outfall opens
detail: Deer Island's 9.5-mile outfall tunnel into Massachusetts Bay opens.

label: Fresh Kills takes last barge
detail: Fresh Kills closes under a 1996 state law, then briefly reopens after September 11 to sort World Trade Center debris.

label: Unfiltered supply upheld
detail: The First Circuit affirms that MWRA may treat its water with ozone instead of building a filtration plant.

label: MetroWest tunnel in service
detail: MWRA's 17.6-mile MetroWest Water Supply Tunnel goes into service, backing up the 1940s Hultman Aqueduct.

label: NYC311 launches
detail: New York's 311 service opens and becomes the model for big-city service desks.

label: Horse manure crisis story first published
detail: Stephen Davies publishes "The Great Horse-Manure Crisis of 1894"; its famous Times quote has never been found.

label: Carroll plant opens
detail: The John J. Carroll Water Treatment Plant in Marlborough begins treating metro Boston's water with ozone.

label: South Korea bans landfilling food waste
detail: Food waste recycling later reaches 95%.

label: GTFS begins in Portland
detail: Google Transit launches with TriMet data, the start of the GTFS transit data format.

label: Big Dig ceiling collapse
detail: About 12 tons of concrete ceiling panels fall in the I-90 connector tunnel, killing Milena Del Valle; the NTSB later blames epoxy creep.

label: New England's all-time peak
detail: The New England grid sets its record peak demand of 28,130 MW, a record that still stands as of October 2026.

label: Big Dig completed
detail: Boston's Central Artery/Tunnel Project, begun in 1991, is completed.

label: Citizens Connect app
detail: Boston's smartphone reporting app lets residents photograph problems with GPS location and get a tracking number.

label: Boston starts LED conversion
detail: Boston begins converting its streetlights to LED in the fall; by 2022 about 85% are LED.

label: Boston water main break
detail: A May 2010 break shows MWRA's metro tunnels need backup and leads to the Metropolitan Water Tunnel Program.

label: Open311 announced
detail: US Federal CIO Vivek Kundra announces a uniform API for 311 service requests.

label: First Wireless Emergency Alert
detail: A National Weather Service flash flood warning near Santa Fe, New Mexico.

label: Living With Water competition
detail: Boston launches a design competition that draws 50 teams from seven countries to redesign sites for seas five feet higher.

label: Massachusetts gas leaks law
detail: A state law creates the Gas System Enhancement Plan to fund replacement of leak-prone gas pipe.

label: Virtual Singapore launched
detail: Singapore's city-scale digital twin starts as part of Smart Nation; completed in 2022.

label: Boston adopts Vision Zero
detail: Boston commits to eliminating traffic deaths by 2030.

label: AMA streetlight guidance
detail: The American Medical Association urges communities to use street lighting of 3000K or lower, citing glare and melatonin suppression.

label: Climate Ready Boston
detail: Boston releases its climate study, projecting about 1.5 feet of sea level rise by 2050 and at least 3 feet after 2070.

label: China launches National Sword
detail: In 2018 China bans many scrap imports and sets a 0.5% contamination limit; US plastic landfilling rises 23.2%.

label: Analyze Boston goes live
detail: Boston's open data portal launches with about 115 datasets.

label: Merrimack Valley gas explosions
detail: Overpressurized gas causes fires and explosions in Lawrence, Andover and North Andover, damaging 131 structures and killing one person.

label: FCC small cell order
detail: The FCC sets 60- and 90-day shot clocks and fee limits for small cell permits.

label: NYC passes Commercial Waste Zones law
detail: Local Law 199 divides the city into 20 zones with three authorized carters each.

label: Boston Zero Waste Plan
detail: Boston sets a target of 80% diversion by 2035, up from about 25%.

label: NTSB finds probable cause
detail: The NTSB blames Columbia Gas' weak management and a low-pressure system without adequate overpressure protection.

label: CopenHill ski slope opens
detail: A ski slope opens on the roof of Copenhagen's Amager Bakke waste-to-energy plant.

label: Sidewalk Labs exits Quayside
detail: Sidewalk Labs pulls out of Toronto's 12-acre waterfront project, citing economic uncertainty.

label: Boston bans city facial surveillance
detail: The City Council votes unanimously to ban city use of facial surveillance.

label: Infrastructure law enacted
detail: The IIJA authorizes $1.2 trillion, including $550 billion in new funding.

label: Purple streetlights appear
detail: Reports of LED streetlights turning purple from phosphor failure begin; by 2022 they come from at least 30 US states.

label: NYC ordered to install accessible signals
detail: A federal court orders New York City to install accessible pedestrian signals at 10,000 intersections within 10 years and at all signalized intersections by 2036.

label: Boston curbside food waste pilot
detail: Boston starts free curbside food waste collection for 10,000 households.

label: Boston's first faux-gas LED
detail: Boston installs its first LED lamp designed to look like a gas lantern, in Bay Village.

label: 988 goes live
detail: The US Suicide and Crisis Lifeline gets a three-digit number.

label: FTA releases MBTA safety findings
detail: The Federal Transit Administration finds the MBTA shifted resources from operations and maintenance to capital projects and issues special directives.

label: Green Line Extension completed
detail: The Medford Branch opens, completing the 4.3-mile, seven-station GLX after the Union Square Branch opened in March.

label: National CSO Inventory
detail: EPA first publishes its National CSO Inventory, which counts about 700 US communities with combined sewers.

label: MUTCD 11th edition
detail: FHWA publishes the final rule for the 11th edition of the US traffic control rulebook, effective January 18, 2024.

label: Electric boiler for Boston steam
detail: Vicinity Energy completes a 42 MW electric boiler at Kendall in Cambridge for the Boston-Cambridge steam system.

label: FCC NG911 order
detail: The FCC requires carriers to deliver 911 calls in IP format on request from 911 authorities.

label: Boston bus signal priority pilot
detail: Boston and the MBTA begin signal priority for routes 57 and 66 on Brighton Avenue; bus waiting at red lights falls 21%.

label: Boston Rodent Action Plan
detail: Boston adopts a multi-department rat plan that prioritizes sanitation over poison.

label: US V2X deployment plan
detail: USDOT releases a national plan targeting V2X at 25% of signalized intersections in the 75 largest metro areas by 2028.

label: MBTA tap-to-ride launches
detail: Contactless payment goes live on MBTA buses and Green Line and Mattapan trolleys (announced for Aug. 1).

label: Lead rule finalized
detail: EPA announces the Lead and Copper Rule Improvements, requiring most US systems to replace lead service lines within 10 years.

label: Bus Network Redesign Phase 1
detail: The MBTA launches Frequent Routes 104, 109, 110 and a combined 116.

label: Last MBTA slow zone cleared
detail: The MBTA removes its final slow zone, down from 233 counted in September 2023.

label: First NYC commercial waste zone complete
detail: Queens Central becomes the first fully implemented commercial waste zone.

label: ASCE grade C
detail: ASCE gives US infrastructure an overall C, its highest grade since the report card began.

label: Tideway opened
detail: King Charles III officially opens London's Thames Tideway Tunnel, fully operational since February 2025.

label: Washington becomes seventh EPR state
detail: Days after Maryland became the sixth, Washington enacts packaging EPR.

label: Highest New England peak in a decade
detail: Demand hits 26,586 MW at 97 degrees F, and reserves run short for more than three hours without outages.

label: US grid batteries near 52 GW
detail: US utility-scale battery capacity reaches nearly 52 GW by mid-2026, with 14 GW more planned for the second half of the year.

label: Red Line car shells released
detail: US Customs and Border Protection releases Red Line car shells held for nearly 10 months under a forced-labor review.

label: MUTCD Revision 1
detail: Revision 1 of the 11th edition is published and takes effect, after the January 18, 2026 state adoption deadline.

label: Boston FY27 budget passed
detail: The council passes a $4.9 billion operating budget and a $4.4 billion five-year capital plan funding 321 projects (date approximate, per WBUR report).

label: IIJA authorities expire
detail: Federal infrastructure law program authorities reach their expiry date; a Senate bill would extend many to December 11, 2026.

label: Lead rule argued in court
detail: Oral argument is held in the D.C. Circuit in AWWA v. EPA, the utility challenge to the lead rule.

label: Lead line deadline
detail: Deadline under the LCRI for most US water systems to finish replacing lead service lines.
